newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 11.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 11.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 index of leading shares finished at its sixth consecutive record close but well short of its new all-time peak as Wall Street inspired British shares to ascend new heights and then dragged them back down to earth.

The FTSE soared to a record 4,466.3 points within minutes of opening, on the back of Monday's 78-point Dow advance. But Wall Street appeared to falter when it opened on Tuesday, and when the Dow turned back after failing to breach 7,100 points, the FTSE also gave up most of the day's gains. It ended 6.9 points firmer at 4,444.3.

FRANKFURT - Bulls continued to hold sway on the German share market, as the DAX index surged in bourse trade to end the session at its second record closing high in a row. The DAX ended up 24.52 points at 3,460.59 points, having earlier hit a record intraday high of 3,474.98 and dealers said that an imminent breach of its next key resistance level at 3,500 was on the cards. In post-bourse trade the index rose 4.18 to 3,430.95.

PARIS - French shares ended lower after a gust of profit-taking took the Paris bourse lower in late afternoon trading. Traders said a slip in the dollar versus the mark, later corrected, sent a signal for investors to book profits on some of the market's recent strong rise. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 23.06 points at 2,686.15.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended little changed with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) breaking off a four-day record run to end slightly below its Monday close. The fact that the SMI ended lower despite an early trading record of 4,734.1 points showed how nervous the market was at current levels, a dealer said. Profit- taking and early Wall Street weakness were seen behind the weaker close. The All-share SPI closed up 1.29 points to 2,9060.32.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's key index ended higher even though participants focused on reports of another major Japanese firm's suspected links with "sokaiya" racketeers.

Japanese media reports of a police investigation into food and seasonings maker Ajinomoto Co, coming soon after a case involving Nomura Securities, had only a limited impact on the market. The Nikkei 225 average closed up 153.83 points at 18,267.72.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks erased the session's gains to end weaker, with investors selling down property stocks and turning their attention to second line counters, analysts said. The Hang Seng Index fell 16.56 points to 13,252.20 after rising to a session high of 13,342.46.

SYDNEY - A mixed Australian share market ended in firmer territory but well off its early Dow-inspired highs as enthusiasm abated. The All Ordinaries index added 6.4 points to 2,468.3 after touching an intraday high of 2,476.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares continued their recent rally, ending solidly up as Wednesday's budget loomed over the market. The all-share index rose 70.7 points to 7,162.0 as the industrials index added 57.7 points to 8,384.7. The golds index put on 37.1 points to 1,441.4.
